Final judged ranking confirmed as: 1) The North Arcade - 98, 2) Luna Valencia - 96, 3) Aisha Bloom - 95, 4) Kairo Saint - 94, 5) Ember District - 93, 6) Naomi Vale - 92, 7) Sol Echo - 91, 8) Maren Wilde - 90, 9) Cedar & Glass - 89, 10) Juno Meridian - 88. 2025 Global Music Awards Judging Committee Summary

Final Top Ten Rankings
1. Luna Valencia — 98
2. The North Arcade — 96
3. Aisha Bloom — 95
4. Kairo Saint — 94
5. Ember District — 93
6. Naomi Vale — 92
7. Sol Echo — 91
8. Maren Wilde — 90
9. Cedar & Glass — 89
10. Juno Meridian — 88

Committee Notes
This year's decisions heavily favored cross-genre experimentation, standout live-performance consistency, and albums with strong narrative cohesion. Judges repeatedly highlighted artists who paired ambitious production with emotional clarity and distinctive songwriting. Several close scores reflected how competitive the field was at the top, especially among artists blending electronic, indie, and Latin influences.

2025 GLOBAL MUSIC AWARDS
Top Ten Artists — Judging Committee Summary
============================================

FINAL RANKINGS
--------------

 1. Luna Valencia         Score: 98
 2. The North Arcade      Score: 96
 3. Aisha Bloom           Score: 95
 4. Kairo Saint           Score: 94
 5. Ember District        Score: 93
 6. Naomi Vale            Score: 92
 7. Sol Echo              Score: 91
 8. Maren Wilde           Score: 90
 9. Cedar & Glass         Score: 89
10. Juno Meridian         Score: 88

--------------------------------------------
EDITORIAL COMMENTARY: KEY TRENDS OF 2025
--------------------------------------------

This year's Global Music Awards reflected a judging landscape shaped by
three defining priorities:

1. Cross-Genre Experimentation
   The top-scoring artists consistently broke free of single-genre
   conventions. The committee placed significant weight on artists who
   wove together electronic, indie, and Latin influences into cohesive
   bodies of work — a standard that Luna Valencia set emphatically at
   the summit with a near-perfect score of 98.

2. Live-Performance Consistency
   Standout performances on stage were a key differentiator in a highly
   competitive field. Artists who translated studio ambition into
   compelling, reliable live experiences — such as The North Arcade
   (96) and Aisha Bloom (95) — were rewarded with top-three finishes.

3. Narrative Cohesion & Emotional Clarity
   Judges repeatedly praised albums that told a clear, emotionally
   resonant story from start to finish. Ambitious production was valued
   only when it served distinctive songwriting — a criterion that
   separated the top ten from the broader field and kept the scoring
   tightly clustered between 88 and 98.

The razor-thin margins across the ranking (just ten points separating
first place from tenth) underscore how competitive the 2025 class was.
The committee noted that several of the lower-ranked artists could have
topped the list in prior years, a testament to the extraordinary depth
of talent in this cycle.

--------------------------------------------
Source: 2025 Global Music Awards Judging Committee

Prepared: 2026-10-31
